2609.17310.title: Zero-shot narrative detection in social messaging
2609.17310.paper_summary: This study investigates the zero-shot ability of large language models (LLMs) to identify and classify hidden narratives in social messages. Our research hypothesis is that LLMs' extensive contextual knowledge allows them to interpret messages on a deeper, pragmatic level, going beyond basic sentiment or topic analysis. Experiments on the Dipromats and SemEval datasets show that providing models with human-written narrative descriptions significantly improves performance, without the need of training examples. In contrast, automatically generated descriptions or the use of few examples (few-shot) often degrade accuracy due to subtle shifts in framing. The study also finds that ensemble methods, particularly majority voting, enhance robustness and that larger models perform best while also being less sensitive to prompt variations. The findings validate that LLMs can effectively detect strategic narratives in a zero-shot setting, and when combined with simple ensembling and human-written descriptions, they can rival supervised systems, offering a scalable solution for narrative detection, specially when there is no training data for the vast majority of domains.
2609.17310.paper_summary_zh: 這項研究探討大型語言模型（LLMs）在零樣本情境下識別和分類社會信息中隱藏敘事的能力。<lb/>我們的研究假設是，LLMs 廣泛的上下文知識使它們能夠在更深層次的實用層面上解釋信息，超越基本的情感或主題分析。<lb/>在 Dipromats 和 SemEval 數據集上的實驗顯示，提供模型人類撰寫的敘事描述顯著提高了性能，而無需訓練示例。<lb/>相比之下，自動生成的描述或使用少量示例（少樣本）往往因框架的微妙變化而降低準確性。<lb/>研究還發現，集成方法，特別是多數投票，增強了穩健性，而較大的模型表現最佳，同時對提示變化的敏感性較低。<lb/>這些發現驗證了 LLMs 在零樣本環境中能有效檢測戰略敘事，並且當與簡單的集成和人類撰寫的描述結合時，它們可以與監督系統相媲美，提供一種可擴展的敘事檢測解決方案，特別是在大多數領域沒有訓練數據的情況下。
